title: Stalks of the direct image of an abelian sheaf on a closed subspace
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $Z\subseteq X$ a closed subset with its subspace topology, $i:Z\to X$ the inclusion, and $F$ an abelian sheaf on $Z$ [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Stalks $F_x$, germs and the induced stalk maps $\varphi_x$ of a morphism $\varphi$ are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], an abelian sheaf being a sheaf of modules over the constant presheaf of rings $\mathbb Z$. Define the abelian sheaf $i_*F$ by $(i_*F)(U)=F(U\cap Z)$ for open $U\subseteq X$. Then $(i_*F)_x=0$ for every $x\in X\setminus Z$, and for every $z\in Z$ the canonical germ map $(i_*F)_z\to F_z$ is a natural isomorphism of abelian groups, compatible with morphisms of abelian sheaves on $Z$.

proof.text: Outside C, use TopCat.Presheaf.exists_le_germ_eq to represent any stalk element on an open V contained in the open complement of C. The inverse image of V under the inclusion is empty. TopCat.Sheaf.isTerminalOfEqEmpty and IsTerminal.isZero show that its section group is zero; its germ is therefore zero. AddCommGrpCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton turns this into IsZero of the stalk.

On C, apply Mathlib TopCat.Presheaf.stalkPushforward.stalkPushforward_iso_of_isInducing to Topology.IsInducing.subtypeVal. This is the cofinal-neighborhood comparison of the source, already proved in Mathlib for all presheaves.

For naturality, apply TopCat.Presheaf.stalk_hom_ext. Precompose each composite with a germ, then rewrite using stalkFunctor_map_germ_assoc, stalkPushforward_germ and stalkFunctor_map_germ. Both sides become the component of the original sheaf morphism on the inverse-image open followed by its germ, definitionally equal.
